title: [observability] an input the engine gives the agent mid-turn (a queued_command attachment, its only transcript line) takes its marker, so message_not_taken no longer fires and stays open for every input to a busy worker (GitHub #66 part 1)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 214 [observability] (GitHub #66 part 1; owner t481u triage, lead-mac 16:15; author rev-h; readers rev-i, then rev-k): an input typed while the agent works is taken.

Base: live main a599100c.

Where things stand. When Spawn types into a session whose agent is mid-turn, the engine (Claude Code 2.1.32x) gives the input to the agent at its next step and writes it ONLY as a transcript line {"type":"attachment","attachment":{"type":"queued_command","commandMode":"prompt","prompt":"<text>\n\n[spawn message #<id>]", ...}}. No user line repeats it (seen on this host: a session's 7 queued_command lines, 0 user lines with the same text). crates/spawn-core/src/ingest.rs claude_line reads such an attachment only for the jobs it ends; markers are read from user lines alone (user_text -> taken). So no message.taken is recorded for any input to a busy worker: message_not_taken fires after SPAWN_MESSAGE_TAKEN_SECS and stays open until the session ends (the issue: 20 open at once, read_since_typed 0..39).

What changes (spawn-core ingest; docs/fleet-architecture.md "Taken"; no store or schema change):
(1) A queued_command attachment whose commandMode is "prompt" takes the markers its prompt holds (string or text blocks), as a user line does: one message.taken {command_id} per marker, keyed <uuid>:taken:<id>. It starts no turn (no message.received).
(2) A queued_command of any other mode (a job's task-notification) is the engine's text: it still ends its jobs and takes nothing, even when it quotes a marker. Sub-agent lines stay ignored.
(3) The clear rule stays the marker: the issue's read_since_typed > 0 suggestion is not taken, since transcript lines after a typing can be the agent's own output.

Done when: rsi/scenarios/214.sh passes (fails with 1 on the base: A is never taken and its alert opens); spawn-core's unit test an_input_given_mid_turn_takes_its_message_and_starts_no_turn; 045 and 138 still pass.
